# Methods

## Design and data

This retrospective observational study used all EuroLeague games from the 2016–17 to the 2024–25 season (`{python} A["seasons"]` seasons, `{python} n(A["games"])` games, `{python} A["games_per_season_min"]`–`{python} A["games_per_season_max"]` per season; the 2019–20 season was interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic and 2020–21 was largely played without spectators). Official box scores, play-by-play logs, shot coordinates and the player registry (height, registered position: guard, forward or centre) were retrieved from the public EuroLeague application programming interface. The data comprised `{python} n(A["player_games"])` player-game records, `{python} n(A["shots"])` field-goal attempts with coordinates and `{python} n(A["assist_edges"])` assisted field goals with identified passer and scorer. Only publicly available performance data were used, so ethical approval was not required. Reporting follows the STROBE statement for observational studies where applicable.

Player-seasons were included when the player was on the roster for at least 10 games and played at least 90 minutes in the season (`{python} n(A["player_seasons"])` player-seasons, `{python} A["players"]` players). Roles were estimated on player-seasons with at least 400 minutes (`{python} n(RF["fit_N"])` player-seasons from `{python} RF["fit_oyuncu_N"]` players) and then assigned to all included player-seasons.

## Lineup segments

Five-on-five lineup segments were reconstructed from play-by-play substitution events, with starting lineups taken from the box score; a new segment started at every substitution by either team. Segments in which both teams had exactly five identified players and that lasted at least 10 s covered `{python} pct(A["stint_minutes_covered"], 1)` of playing time (`{python} n(A["stints"])` segments). Possessions per segment were estimated as field-goal attempts + 0.44 × free-throw attempts − offensive rebounds + turnovers [@kubatko2007starting], averaged over the two teams. Lineup models used all complete five-on-five segments with at least one estimated possession (`{python} n(M5["segment_N"])` segments). Segment net rating was defined as the home-minus-away point difference per 100 possessions.

## Role variables

Variables were chosen to describe what a player does rather than how well he does it, so that roles would not be confounded with player quality: shooting efficiency, composite valuation indices and height were not used. Three groups of `{python} len(RF["degiskenler"])` variables were computed. (1) Possession shares, with denominators equal to the team and opponent totals accumulated while the player was on court in the lineup segments: usage, assist, offensive and defensive rebound, steal, block and turnover percentages, fouls drawn per team possession and fouls committed per opponent possession, three-point attempt rate and free-throw rate. (2) Shot profile: proportions of field-goal attempts at the rim (≤ 1.25 m), in the paint (1.25–3 m) and from mid-range, the corner share of three-point attempts, and the fast-break and second-chance shares of attempts. (3) Assist network: the shares of a player's assists that led to three-point attempts, to shots within 3 m and to registered centres, the diversity of assist recipients (normalised Shannon entropy), the proportions of made two- and three-point field goals that were assisted, and the share of received assists that came from guards. Strongly redundant variables (overall assisted share; assists relative to assists plus made field goals) were removed. Right-skewed assist, offensive-rebound, steal and block percentages were square-root transformed. All variables were standardised within season using the mean and standard deviation of the estimation sample; there were no missing values in the estimation sample, and missing values in lower-minute player-seasons were set to the season mean.

## Number of roles

Gaussian mixture models were fitted with scikit-learn 1.9.1 (five initialisations, regularisation 10^-4^ added to the covariance diagonal). Diagonal and tied (shared full) covariance structures were compared by the Bayesian information criterion, and the structure with the lower average criterion across four to eight roles (`{python} COV`) was retained; unconstrained covariance matrices were not used because their number of parameters would exceed the sample size. For four to eight roles we computed the silhouette coefficient and the bootstrap stability of each cluster as the mean maximum Jaccard similarity between the original cluster and the clusters found in bootstrap resamples [@hennig2007cluster]. Resampling was done at the player level, keeping all of a player's seasons together (`{python} RF["Bscan"]` resamples for the scan, `{python} RF["B"]` for the final solutions). Following Hennig, values ≥ 0.75 were taken to indicate a stable cluster and values ≤ 0.5 a dissolved cluster. Stability over time was assessed by fitting the model on 2016–2019 and on 2020–2024 and comparing their assignments for players who first appeared after 2019 (adjusted Rand index). The decision rule, fixed before the final solution was examined, was to retain the number of roles with the highest mean Jaccard among solutions whose least stable cluster was above 0.5, preferring the solution with better temporal agreement when mean Jaccard values differed by 0.02 or less. All player-seasons were assigned to the role with the highest posterior probability. Because the variable set was refined during exploratory analyses, the final solution was compared with solutions from alternative variable sets (box-score rates only; box-score rates plus shot profile; possession shares plus shot profile; and the final set plus height) using bootstrap stability and the adjusted Rand index. The seven-cluster Ward solution previously derived from these data in the author's doctoral thesis was reproduced and evaluated with the same player-level bootstrap.

## Roles and registered positions

The association between roles and registered positions was quantified with Cramér's V, with a 95% confidence interval from a player-level bootstrap (`{python} RF["B"]` resamples), and with the share of each role belonging to its most frequent position.

## Roles and lineup performance

Individual player quality was estimated with regularised adjusted plus-minus (RAPM): a ridge regression of segment net rating on indicators for the ten players on court (+1 home, −1 away), weighted by possessions, with an intercept for home advantage [@grassetti2020extended; @petridis2026lineup]. Players with fewer than 300 possessions shared one replacement-level coefficient, and players not seen in the training data were set to the league average. The penalty was chosen by five-fold cross-validation with games as groups.

RAPM was fitted on 2016–2022 and its residuals were regressed on the home-minus-away difference in the number of players in each role and in all pairwise role products, including same-role pairs coded as the number of pairs within the lineup (`{python} M5["rol_bilesimi"]["terim_N"]` terms for five roles). The ridge penalty of this composition model was chosen by game-grouped cross-validation within the training data. The gain in possession-weighted R² over RAPM alone was evaluated on 2023–2024 segments. Its null distribution was obtained by permuting role labels among player-seasons within season (`{python} n(M5["rol_bilesimi"]["B"])` permutations), which preserves player quality and lineup structure while removing role information. The same analysis was repeated with the four-role solution from the same variable set. To quantify the power of this test, synergy effects of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 point per 100 possessions were added to the observed net ratings for every co-occurrence of the most frequent pair of different roles, RAPM and the composition model were refitted, and the proportion of `{python} P["sim"]` simulations in which the permutation test (`{python} P["B"]` permutations) gave *p* < .05 was recorded.

## Sensitivity analysis: role-combination tests

To examine an analysis commonly used to link roles with success, which was also used in the thesis, we selected role combinations (sets of five archetypes from the thesis's seven-cluster solution) whose mean lineup-game net rating per 40 minutes differed from zero (one-sample *t* test, *p* < .05, at least 10 lineup-games) and tested the distribution of archetypes among them with a chi-square goodness-of-fit test against their share of playing time. We compared this naive test with a permutation test that repeated the whole selection procedure after shuffling net ratings within team-season blocks (`{python} n(F2T["permutasyon"]["B"])` permutations), with and without a minimum lineup-game duration of 2 minutes, and counted the combinations surviving Benjamini–Hochberg correction.
